ai.title: Fix image path extraction in messages
ai.summary: Image path extraction now handles bare relative paths and prevents agent mention regex from corrupting file paths containing slashes. Regex updates add support for `assets/image.png` style paths and expand trailing punctuation stripping. Covers `client.ts` and `utils/image-handler.ts` in npm-app.

eli5.text: When you include an image path in your message like 'assets/image.png', the assistant now correctly recognizes it as a file path instead of mistaking it for an @agent mention and corrupting the path. Previously, paths without the standard markdown format or paths containing slashes could get mangled when processed alongside agent mentions. For example, a bare path like 'assets/image.png' embedded anywhere in your message would now be extracted properly, and existing paths that contain slashes won't have their format altered by the mention-handling logic. The fix applies to image path extraction throughout messages in the npm-app component and is live today.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.489 in release package
ai.summary: Freebuff is released as version 1.0.489. The bump follows a fix in which image path extraction now handles bare relative paths and prevents the agent-mention regex from corrupting paths containing slashes, supporting `assets/image.png`-style input across the npm-app client. No structural code changes ship in 1.0.489 itself; the release increments only the version identifier in `npm-app/release/package.json`.
ai.evidence: npm-app/release/package.json: version field changed from "1.0.488" to "1.0.489"; this is a release-bump commit (+1/-1 lines) with no functional changes, paired with a prior image path-extraction fix in npm-app.

eli5.text: This release makes image handling more reliable. When you include pictures in your conversations, the system now correctly understands and preserves image file paths, even when they are written in simpler relative formats like assets/image.png. It also stops the system from mistakenly altering file paths that contain slashes or special characters, so your image references stay intact throughout the conversation. Upgrading means fewer errors when working with images, and your file paths won't get corrupted by automated text processing.

ai.title: Automatic image descriptions added to CLI uploads
ai.summary: CLI image upload now injects text parts listing filenames (e.g. `[Attached Image: image_1.png]`) alongside binary image data. This ensures the model receives context about attached files. The change affects `npm-app/src/cli.ts` message construction and `npm-app/src/utils/image-handler.ts` regex to ignore `@` prefixed paths.

eli5.text: When you attach an image to a message in the CLI, the assistant now sees a note like '[Attached Image: image_1.png]' alongside the image data, so it's not totally in the dark about what you sent. The image path detection also ignores any paths starting with '@', which stops those from being mistakenly treated as uploaded files. You won't see this text yourself unless you're inspecting the internal message format, but the assistant now has a label to reference when discussing your attachment.

ai.summary: Bumped the codebuff npm package version from 1.0.489 to 1.0.490 in `npm-app/release/package.json`. This is a release-only commit with no functional or structural code modifications. The increment precedes the automatic image descriptions feature shipped in this release cycle.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies `npm-app/release/package.json`, incrementing the `version` field from `1.0.489` to `1.0.490`, with the only changed lines being the version string and no other structural or functional modifications in the provided hunk. eli5.text: This release improves how images are shared with Freebuff through the command line, making image uploads clearer and more reliable. When you attach an image to your terminal chat, Freebuff now automatically includes a text note naming the image file, so the AI can better understand what you have added, for example by reading 'Attached Image: screenshot_3.png' alongside the picture. It also handles image paths more smoothly, correctly recognizing files that start with an @ symbol without errors. Upgrading means your image attachments will come with helpful labels by default, giving the AI more context about your files and making your conversations with Freebuff more accurate and informative.

ai.title: StreamChunk typed union replaces raw string stream in backend LLM
ai.summary: New StreamChunk union type (text, reasoning, error) replaces raw string AsyncGenerator yields in promptAiSdkStream, processStreamWithTools, and processStreamWithTags. Reasoning deltas now flow as typed chunks instead of being serialized into think_deeply tool-call text at the source. Error chunks yield and return rather than throwing, preventing unhandled stream aborts. Internal refactor across backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts, backend/src/tools/stream-parser.ts, and backend/src/xml-stream-parser.ts; tool-tag serialization moved downstream to stream-parser.

eli5.text: The backend that powers the AI assistant now tags each piece of a streaming reply with a label (text, reasoning, or error) instead of sending everything as a plain string. If you watch a reply come in live, you won't see a different appearance, but internally the assistant can now separate its own thinking process from the words it shows you, and if something goes wrong mid-stream the assistant stops cleanly instead of crashing the connection. This is already live for anyone using the assistant through the affected backend path.

ai.title: Add manual stop sequence detection for AI SDK streams
ai.summary: Added `StopSequenceHandler` to manually detect and truncate streams based on stop sequences, replacing reliance on upstream API support. This ensures precise control over output termination in `promptAiSdkStream`. The change affects `common/src/util/stop-sequence.ts` and `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts`. The handler buffers text chunks to identify overlaps, yielding only text preceding the stop sequence.

eli5.text: Starting today, the system that sends back AI replies now watches each chunk of text itself and cuts the reply off the moment a predetermined stop marker appears, instead of waiting for the upstream AI service to do it. This affects you if you are streaming a response through the core prompt path, because the new manual stop-sequence handler now controls exactly where the streamed text ends. If you watched closely you would notice the reply stops mid-stream right at your configured stop sequence, with no extra trailing text, and any buffered text up to that point is still flushed out before the stream closes.

ai.title: Simplify backend buildUserMessageContent logic
ai.summary: Refactored `buildUserMessageContent` in `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts` to stop merging prompt/params with client-provided `content` parts. The function now returns `content` arrays as-is, assuming the client (npm-app) already combined them, and only constructs text strings when `content` is absent. This removes ~19 lines of redundant part-prepending logic.

eli5.text: The system that prepares your messages has been simplified so it no longer duplicates work already done by the program that sends your files and text. If you send a mix of text and images, the messages will now be assembled exactly as the sender provided them, without the system reordering or merging parts behind the scenes. This is a live change you won't notice visually, but it keeps message preparation consistent between the two parts of the program.

ai.title: Fix broken tests by updating mock stream yields to typed objects
ai.summary: Updated mock implementations in backend integration and unit tests to yield typed text objects (`{ type: 'text', text: ... }`) instead of raw strings. This aligns test mocks with the current `promptAiSdkStream` interface expectations. Affected files include `cost-aggregation.integration.test.ts`, `loop-agent-steps.test.ts`, `main-prompt.test.ts`, `read-docs-tool.test.ts`, `run-agent-step-tools.test.ts`, `web-search-tool.test.ts`, and `xml-stream-parser.test.ts`. Assertion logic in `xml-stream-parser.test.ts` was also adjusted to extract text from the new object structure.

eli5.text: The tests that check the assistant's backend were failing because the mock data they use to simulate the assistant's responses had the wrong format. The test helpers were sending plain text, but the real system now expects each piece of text wrapped in an object with a type label and the text itself. The fix updates all those mock responses to match the new expected structure so the tests pass again. If you looked at the test files, you would see the mock responses now return objects like { type: 'text', text: '...' } instead of just the raw string. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping that only affects what the developers see when they run the automated tests; it changes nothing about the assistant's actual behavior.

ai.title: Save this agent button on agent detail page
ai.summary: New SaveAgentButton component added to the agent detail page. It copies the command `codebuff save-agent <agentId>` to the clipboard and shows a toast. The button sits alongside CopyIdButton and RunAgentButton in web/src/app/publishers/[id]/agents/[agentId]/[version]/page.tsx.

eli5.text: On your agent detail page, when you view a specific agent, there is now a new "Save this agent" button sitting next to the existing "Copy ID" and "Run agent" buttons. Clicking it copies the text “codebuff save-agent [agent-id]” to your clipboard and shows a small notification confirming the copy. The button appears for anyone viewing the agent detail page and is active today.

ai.title: New codebuff save-agent CLI command
ai.summary: Added `codebuff save-agent` command to append agent IDs to `addedSpawnableAgents` in `codebuff.json`. Implements `handleSaveAgent` in `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/save-agent.ts` to parse args, update config via `loadRawCodebuffConfig`, and report new/existing agents. Registered command in `npm-app/src/index.ts` and updated `isCommand` check to prevent treating it as initial input. Helper `loadRawCodebuffConfig` added to `npm-app/src/json-config/parser.ts` to read raw JSONC config.

eli5.text: You can now run a new terminal command that adds one or more assistant IDs to the list of assistants a project is allowed to call. Running the command prints which IDs were newly added and which were already on the list, and it updates the project's settings file directly. Nothing else in the project setup is touched, so existing settings stay in place. The feature is available today through the command line.

ai.title: Add addedSpawnableAgents and removedSpawnableAgents to codebuff.json
ai.summary: Added `addedSpawnableAgents` and `removedSpawnableAgents` fields to `codebuff.json` to manage base subagents. `CodebuffConfigSchema` updated to `looseObject` with new optional string arrays. `main-prompt.ts` logic merges added agents and filters removed agents when `--agent` is unspecified. Default config includes new fields as undefined.

eli5.text: The assistant can now be told which helper tools it is allowed to bring in or keep out of a project, all from one easy-to-edit settings file. When you don't pick a specific helper yourself, the system first builds the normal list, then adds any extras you listed and removes any you crossed out, giving you a simple add-and-remove list instead of rewriting the whole roster each time. That add-and-remove switch is already in the sample settings file, and the git-helper tool named there is now expected to join projects using these settings today.

ai.title: Codebuff version bumped to 1.0.491
ai.summary: The `codebuff` package version in `npm-app/release/package.json` has been incremented from 1.0.490 to 1.0.491 as part of the standard release process. This release encompasses several notable updates including the introduction of the StreamChunk typed union replacing raw string streams in the backend LLM layer, manual stop sequence detection for AI SDK streams, a new SaveAgentButton component and `codebuff save-agent` CLI command, and schema additions of `addedSpawnableAgents`/`removedSpawnableAgents` fields to `codebuff.json`. Additionally, backend build logic was simplified, and integration tests were updated to align with the new stream typing.
ai.evidence: Diff shows a single-line version field change in `npm-app/release/package.json` from `1.0.490` to `1.0.491`. This is a release-bump commit (Commit nature: release-bump) with stats of +1/-1, modifying only the version string in the codebuff package manifest.

eli5.text: This release introduces a new way to save and manage AI agent helpers directly from your browser or terminal, making it easier to keep your favorite assistants handy for future coding tasks. You can now click a "Save Agent" button on any agent's detail page to instantly add it to your project's configuration via a simple command, and the system now tracks which agents you have added or removed so your setup stays organized. The underlying streaming of AI responses has been rebuilt to be more reliable and precise, giving you cleaner, more accurate output with fewer interruptions and better control over when responses stop. You also gain finer control over your agent toolkit through an updated config file that lets you add or remove specific subagents when you run your main assistant. Upgrading means smoother, more dependable interactions with saved agents and smarter handling of how AI text and reasoning flow through your terminal.

ai.title: Fix 404 errors in documentation internal links
ai.summary: Resolved 404 errors by correcting internal documentation links. Updated anchor references in `claude-code-comparison.mdx` and related files to ensure accurate navigation. Scope includes web content and evaluation fixtures. Specific fix involved removing trailing question marks from anchor IDs like `#what-models-do-you-use?`.

eli5.text: If you clicked a link in the documentation that took you to a page that said "404 Not Found," that broken link has now been fixed. Several cross-references between help articles and guides were pointing to slightly wrong spots, often just an extra character or a misspelled address, so the tool trimmed or corrected those addresses until the links landed on the right page again. You don't need to do anything; the next time you click one of those in-document links, it will go straight to the section you wanted instead of erroring out.

ai.title: SDK build drops ESM output, ships CommonJS only
ai.summary: Removed ESM build steps and dual-format output from `sdk/build.ts`, consolidating artifacts into a single CommonJS `dist` directory. Updated `sdk/package.json` to set `type` to `commonjs`, point `main`/`types` to `./dist/`, and remove `import`/`module` export conditions. Deleted ESM-specific smoke tests in `sdk/smoke-test-dist.ts` and adjusted `tsconfig.build.json` output path.

eli5.text: You now download a single version of the code library (CommonJS) instead of two (ESM and CommonJS). The ESM version, which some tools preferred for modern setups, has been removed, so the package now ships only the CommonJS format in a simplified directory. If you integrate the library, your project will no longer find the ESM entry points and must use CommonJS imports instead, even if your project is configured for the newer module style.

ai.title: Update SDK README API key URL and clarify examples
ai.summary: Update `sdk/README.md` to reflect new Codebuff API key URL (`/api-keys`). Add comments explaining `handleEvent` behavior and `previousRun` usage in code examples. Clarify custom agent creation context.

eli5.text: If you're using the assistant SDK to build custom workflows, the place where you get your API key has moved to a simpler web address (codebuff.com/api-keys instead of the old profile page link). The example code snippets in the guide now include brief notes explaining what each part does, like how event logging captures every step of a run, and how to chain one run to an earlier one. These are just documentation tweaks, so nothing about how the assistant actually works changed.

ai.title: SDK publish script migrated to bun run scripts/publish.ts
ai.summary: SDK package.json scripts prepare-dist and publish-sdk now invoke bun run scripts/publish.ts instead of node scripts/publish.js. The publish script was renamed from .js to .ts, maintaining 100% similarity. This aligns the publish workflow with the rest of the SDK build tooling that uses bun. Note that the publish-dry-run script still references the old node scripts/publish.js path.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes script that packages and ships the SDK now runs on the same modern toolkit (Bun) as the rest of the build process, instead of the older Node-based runner. This is internal housekeeping: if you publish or maintain the SDK, the two main packaging commands will now use that faster, newer tool, and the script file itself was renamed from a JavaScript file to a TypeScript file with identical contents. The dry-run command was left pointing at the old path and was not updated, so it still works as before. Nothing live changes for you today; you would only notice this if you run the SDK packaging commands yourself.

ai.title: Drop generic types on customToolDefinitions
ai.summary: Removes generic type parameters <A, B, C> from CodebuffClient.run and customToolDefinitions in sdk/src/client.ts. Simplifies SDK interface by using non-generic CustomToolDefinition. Internal refactor; no runtime behavior change.

eli5.text: If you build your own tools for the assistant and connect them through the software kit, you no longer need to specify exact data shapes for each tool when you define them. The kit now accepts your custom tools with simpler instructions, dropping strict labeling that was required before; this is an internal cleanup that doesn't change how your tools actually run. This is live today for projects using the software kit to plug in their own tools.

ai.title: Skip clientToolCallSchema validation for custom tools
ai.summary: handleToolCall now skips clientToolCallSchema.parse for actions where toolName is not in toolNames. This prevents validation errors when handling custom tool calls. Change scoped to sdk/src/client.ts. Validation now runs only for built-in tools; custom tools bypass schema check.

eli5.text: When you use a custom tool that your assistant app built itself, rather than one of the standard built-in tools, the system now skips a strict format check that used to apply to every tool. You won't see this unless you were getting an error when your custom tool returned a response in an unexpected format: those calls now go through without being validated against the built-in tool schema. This only affects code that developers write to extend the assistant's toolset; the standard tools still get the same validation as before.
